newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Police net biggest ever Dutch Ecstasy haul.
newsitem.headline: Police net biggest ever Dutch Ecstasy haul.

text.p: Police in the Dutch port of Rotterdam said on Sunday they had found a huge haul of illegal chemicals, on board a container ship from China, capable of producing some 30 million Ecstasy pills.
It was the biggest discovery of the illegal chemicals in the country, they said.
"The material was found on the last day of last year and since then we have made three arrests," a police spokesman said.
Police said 3,000 litres of the chemical -- known as BMK (Benzyl Methyl Ketone) had been found in 200-litre drums hidden amongst a shipment of peanut oil from China.

In the course of the investigation, police said it had appeared that around 9,000 litres of the chemical had been imported into the Netherlands from China in the last year, a quantity sufficient to produce some 90 million Ecstasy pills.
BMK is a strictly-controlled material used by the phamaceutical industry. Around five litres are legally imported into the Netherlands every year.
Ecstasy -- a synthetic drug declared illegal in the Netherlands in 1988 -- produces a sense of euphoria among users but is considered highly dangerous.
